candidates.directedText: [measured, unhurried picture-book storytelling] [warmly, with the freshness of morning] In Lanternleaf Forest, morning began with seed bells. [short pause] [with a familiar, musical lift] Their bright chime woke every window and warm oven. [long pause] [allow the warmth to fall into a real hush] But one rain-washed morning, the bells were silent. [long pause] [curious and gently concerned] Fern found their ribbons twisted around the bell tree. [short pause] [with a nimble working rhythm, but never rushed] She loosened the low knots while Pipkin slipped the middle ones free. [long pause] [slowing as the last problem comes into view] Still, the highest ribbon hugged a thorny branch. [long pause] [small disappointment, never helpless] I cannot reach it. [long pause] [bright, confident, and kind] I can, if you show me a path through the thorns. [long pause] [settling, with precise wonder] Fern traced a silver path through the leaves. [long pause] [long pause] [leave a generous silent space for the child to help] [long pause] [return with quiet satisfaction] At the top, Pipkin reached the knotted ribbon. [short pause] [careful and exact] One careful tug opened the knot. [long pause] [opening the voice with the motion] The breeze rushed in. [short pause] [delighted and musical, separating the count] The seed bells bobbed and chimed—one, two, three! [long pause] [let the whole world seem to exhale] All at once, the forest morning opened around them. [long pause] [intimate and sincerely grateful] You reached what I could not. [long pause] [smiling, equally sincere] You saw the way I could not. [long pause] [quietly luminous, like closing a beloved picture book] Above them, the bell tree played the morning they had made together.
